column4: F: A common BricsCAD drawing set. Can it become a model, a schedule and a cost?
column5: F: Here is a common BricsCAD drawing set. Eight sheets: plans, elevations, a beam layout, a truss section. | M: Can it become a model, a schedule and a cost? | F: Let's see. Nothing is marked.

column3: rendered from the DXF by film_dxf2bim_render_sheets.py (title block text filtered)
column5: M: Plain 2D. Lines, hatches and dimensions, drawn for people, not for a database. | F: And what does the Modeller know? | M: Only what each drawing states.

column4: M: It suggests only what the drawing states. In yellow.
column5: M: It suggests only what the drawing states. The units from the file header, the view and the name from the title. | F: Why yellow? | M: Yellow means suggested, not yet yours.

column3: lane §L7.11 (grid from dimension ticks, datum from the ground line)
column4: M: Accept all. The grid comes from the dimension ticks.
column5: M: Accept all. The grid comes from the dimension ticks, not from where a label happens to sit. | F: And the height datum? | M: From the heavy ground line.

column3: lane §L7.11 (SET, LEVEL, PL datum 0.6096 m typed)
column4: M: Three facts only a person can state.
column5: M: Three facts only a person can state. The name of the set, the plan level, and the plinth datum: two feet above ground, read from the column detail. | F: Typed once? | M: Typed once, and kept in the sheet.

column3: W-SHED-CHAIN S1 (eight settings sheets reopened) · lane §L7.12
column4: M: The settings live in the sheets. All eight, reopened.
column5: M: Those settings are saved in the sheets themselves, so all eight sheets reopen together. | F: What is chosen? | M: Which layer is a column, a footing, a beam, a wall panel, a fan, a net, a door swing, a truss bar.

column3: lane §L13.2 (Complete: slab + roof, derived, yellow defaults)
column4: M: Complete adds a slab and a roof, listed as defaults.
column5: M: The drawings imply a floor slab and a roof. Ticking Complete adds them, and lists their thickness as yellow defaults. | F: So they are estimates? | M: Estimates, and marked as such.

column4: M: Convert. Four hundred forty-eight bodies, in their material colours.
column5: M: Convert. Four hundred forty-eight bodies: thirty-two columns, thirty-two footings, thirty-five beams, forty-one wall panels, thirteen fans, three nets, four doors, the truss members and plates, a slab and a roof. | F: Colours? | M: Each material in its standard colour.

column4: M: The usual IFC, then our database. Every mesh keeps its source.
column5: M: Export the usual IFC with its materials. Then the usual extractor, to our database format. | F: What is in it? | M: Four hundred forty-eight elements, eight materials, and for each mesh the sheet and the handle it came from.

column3: W-SHED-CHAIN S4 (Viewer opens the DB: 448 elements, 41 walls)
column4: M: The same database opens in the Viewer.
column5: M: The same database opens in the Viewer, in three dimensions, in the materials' colours. | F: Nothing converted again? | M: Nothing.

column4: M: Find the walls. Forty-one. Pick one.
column5: M: Find the walls: forty-one, as built from the drawings. Pick one and it shows its class, its label from the drawing, and its material.

column4: M: Five D. The cost, from rates and the model's quantities.
column5: M: The five D page: cost by discipline, from the rates and the quantities of the model. | F: A tender? | M: No. A rate based estimate, about one point oh five million dollars.

column3: W-SHED-CHAIN S5 (§SCHEDULE 6 tasks, 194 calendar days, source=generated)
column4: M: Four D. A generated schedule: six tasks, a hundred ninety-four days.
column5: M: Four D: a schedule the Viewer generates when the model has none. Six phases over a hundred and ninety-four calendar days. | F: Whose sequence? | M: A default one. Not this farm's real plan.

column4: M: What is still open, stated.
column5: M: Still open, stated plainly. The truss spacing is not drawn, so the repeated trusses are assumed. The evaporative pads have no length. The cost is an estimate and the schedule a default. | F: And the drawing itself? | M: Every number on screen came from this run.

column4: F: From a drawing to a model.
column5: F: From a common drawing, to a model, a schedule and a cost. | M: Every figure on screen came from this run.
